connections.why: Describing motion depends first on measuring distance, time and velocity correctly
Forces change motion through Newton's second law, F = ma
Weight is the gravitational force acting on a mass
A resultant force changes momentum; impulse equals force times time
Work done is force multiplied by distance moved in the force's direction
Pressure is the force acting per unit area
Pressure in a liquid depends on its density and depth
Internal energy is the kinetic and potential energy of particles
Particle motion explains expansion, heat capacity and changes of state
Temperature differences drive conduction, convection and radiation
Waves transfer energy without transferring matter
Light obeys the general wave rules of reflection and refraction
Sound is a longitudinal wave sharing the general properties of waves
Visible light is one part of the electromagnetic spectrum
Thermal radiation is carried by infrared electromagnetic waves
Moving charges and magnetic fields interact to produce the motor effect and induction
Current, voltage and resistance determine how circuits behave
Understanding current and power explains fuses, earthing and safe wiring
Induced voltages and currents underlie generators and transformers
Generators and transformers transfer energy electrically using induction
Oscillating charges and currents generate electromagnetic waves
Radioactive decay occurs when unstable nuclei emit radiation
Nuclear processes release energy, conserved as in all energy transfers
Gravity governs orbits of planets, moons and satellites
Nuclear fusion powers stars and drives their life cycles
Red-shift of starlight is evidence for an expanding Universe
